title: Architecture & Standards: API, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and standards for API design, code quality, infrastructure provisioning, model-serving practices, observability, and performance SLOs. It is intended for engineers, product owners, and platform teams who implement or operate services that interact with our inference runtime.

Scope:
- Public REST/GRPC/HTTP APIs exposed by Redwood services.
- Backend services that contribute to model-serving (request routing, batching, cache, KV management).
- Infra provisioning patterns for cloud-hosted and private deployment variants.
- Observability requirements and performance SLOs for production services.
- ADR index for major design decisions related to inference routing and failure modes.

Principles (short):
- Consistency: APIs and telemetry must be consistent across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Safety-first: Fail open where appropriate, fail fast where safety requires (quota enforcement, PII blocking).
- Observable: Every new service ships with metrics, logs, traces, and an on-call runbook.
- Cost-aware: Defaults should bias toward predictable cost (rate-limiting, batching recommendations).
- Evolvable: Use explicit versioning and ADRs for breaking changes.

1) API Standards
- Design: Prefer REST/JSON for public-facing endpoints; internal high-throughput links may use gRPC with proto3 definitions. Always provide a single page API contract in OpenAPI v3 format stored in the service repo under /api/openapi.yaml.
- Versioning:
  1. Path-based major versions: /v1/, /v2/ for breaking changes.
  2. Minor changes must be backward compatible; deprecations announced via changelog and console UI 90 days before removal.
- Error model:
  - Use standard HTTP status codes.
  - Response body schema for errors: {"code": string, "message": string, "details": optional object} (include a machine-readable code).
- Rate limits and quotas:
  - All public endpoints must support standard X-RateLimit headers and return 429 when limits exceeded.
  - Default burst policy: 100 rps per API key for self-serve tenants; enterprise tiers configured per contract.
- Authentication & Authorization:
  - Bearer token (JWT opaque token) for hosted API; mutual TLS and API keys for private endpoints per customer contract.
  - Service-to-service calls must use signed short-lived tokens (see infra standards).
- Contract testing:
  - Every client-facing API must include an automated contract test that runs in PRs and CI against a mock server.

2) Coding Standards
- Language & style:
  - Follow idiomatic style guides for the primary language (Go: effective Go + gofmt; Python: PEP8 + Black + Pyright type checks; TypeScript: ESLint + Prettier).
- Testing:
  - Unit tests: >= 90% coverage on new modules.
  - Integration tests: run against a lightweight local stack (docker-compose or test harness) in CI.
  - End-to-end smoke tests: defined and executed nightly for critical workflows (model serving, routing, billing).
- Static analysis:
  - All repos must enable linters and aggregator security scanning (Snyk/Dependabot for dependencies).
- PR requirements:
  - At least one code owner approval and passing CI before merge; large changes require design doc and ADR.

3) Infrastructure Standards
- IaC and environment parity:
  - Terraform for cloud infra; modules stored in infra-terraform/ and versioned.
  - Every environment (dev/stage/prod) must be reproducible with the same modules and distinct variable sets.
- Secrets and key management:
  - Use KMS/HSM-backed secrets (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and never store secrets in plain text.
- Network and tenancy:
  - Private deployment templates include clear VPC, subnet, and firewall/security group rules.
  - Zero-trust segmenting for control plane and data plane in Private deployments.
- Deployment model:
  - Blue/green or canary by default for model-serving control plane changes.
  - For Dedicated GPU pools use rolling restarts with 5% max concurrent disruption.

4) Model-serving Standards
- Model packaging:
  - Models must be provided in a container image with a standardized entrypoint that exposes the runtime endpoint /v1/predict and readiness/liveness endpoints.
  - Include a model.manifest.json at image root containing {"name", "version", "input_shape", "kv_cache_compatible", "quantization_profile"}.
- Runtime compatibility:
  - Runtime supports multiple kernel backends; images must include metadata indicating required ops/kernels.
- Rolling upgrades & fallback:
  - New model versions must be deployed via canary (default 1% traffic), monitored for quality/regression for 24h before ramp.
  - Automatic fallback policy: on >2% error-rate increase or latency P95 breach for 5m, route traffic to previous stable model variant.
- Batching and caching:
  - Services must expose configurable batching windows (e.g. 5ms, 10ms) and a KV cache enablement flag.
  - Defaults: batching=10ms for text generation workloads; adjustable per workload.
- Security & data handling:
  - For any model that processes PII, mark model.manifest.json confidentiality=restricted and enable request audit-logging.

5) Observability Standards
- Metrics:
  - All services export Prometheus-compatible metrics. Standard metric namespace: redwood_<service>_. Examples: redwood_inference_requests_total, redwood_inference_request_latency_seconds (histogram with buckets aligned to SLOs).
  - Required labels: service, region, model, route, deployment_id, shard.
- Tracing:
  - Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry. Every external request must propagate a trace-id. Sampling default: 10% for production, configurable per service.
- Logs:
  - Structured JSON logs (timestamp, level, service, trace_id, span_id, request_id, msg). No raw PII in logs.
- Dashboards & alerts:
  - Per-route dashboards in Grafana with token-level cost breakdown.
  - Alerting: page for SLO breaches (see SLOs below), email for degraded but non-paging conditions.
- On-call & runbooks:
  - Each service must publish a runbook with ownership, escalation path, TL;DR remediation steps, and a postmortem template link.

6) Performance Standards & SLOs
- SLOs (targeted for tenant-facing inference endpoints):
  - Latency: P95 < 250ms, P99 < 800ms for text-generation small models (<= 8k context) on hosted tier. Dedicated tiers should have contractual latency targets documented per SKU.
  - Availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted inference API.
  - Error rate: < 0.5% failed requests (5xx) aggregated monthly.
- Budgeting and monitoring:
  - Error budget tracked in eng-sre dashboards; when budget <25% trigger release freeze and game-day review.
- Load testing:
  - New model variants or infra changes must include a throughput profile and load test results (k6 / vegeta / custom runner) showing steady state QPS and tail latency at target concurrency.

7) Decision Records (ADRs) Index
- ADR-001: Default routing policy — Latency-first then cost fallback (2025-06-12).
- ADR-006: Telemetry schema v1 (2025-11-02).
- ADR-012: Standard model.manifest.json schema (2026-02-10).
- ADR process:
  1. Draft ADR in repo /docs/adrs/ with status {proposed, accepted, deprecated}.
  2. Assign reviewer(s) and target review window (7 business days).
  3. Accepted ADRs are linked in this document and referenced in service READMEs.

8) Onboarding checklist for new services
- [ ] Add OpenAPI spec to /api/openapi.yaml
- [ ] Implement Prometheus metrics and a basic Grafana dashboard
- [ ] Add contract tests and CI checks
- [ ] Provide model.manifest.json (if model-serving)
- [ ] Publish runbook and on-call owner

Appendix A — Standard config examples
- Example model.manifest.json (minimal):
  {
    "name": "redwood-small-llm",
    "version": "2026-01-15",
    "input_shape": "(batch, tokens)",
    "kv_cache_compatible": "true",
    "quantization_profile": "int8-mixed"
  }

- Example Prometheus metric registration (Go):
  promhist := prometheus.NewHistogramVec(prometheus.HistogramOpts{
    Name: "redwood_inference_request_latency_seconds",
    Help: "Request latency seconds",
    Buckets: prometheus.DefBuckets,
  }, []string{"service","region","model","route","deployment_id"})
